Mr. ___ is a ___ with a PMHx of cholangiocarcinoma s/p 
resection ___ c/b cholangitis in ___ s/p biliary stent 
placement, local mets to duodenum s/p duodenal stent placement, 
completed Cyberknife treatment in ___, with recent admission 
for E.coli bacteremia, presented after being found down.
Per report, the patient reports after being found down.
Circumstances are unclear.

The patient was oriented but a poor 
historian and in the ED he was unable to recall what led him to 
being found on the ground.

Per collateral obtained in the ED, his ex-wife states that the 
patient has been unable to perform his ADLs at home, she has 
been stopping by multiple times to help feed, bath and dress 
him.

She states he has difficulty ambulating under his own power 
and is not safe at home.
ROS: 10-point ROS negative except as noted above in HPI

He was recently admitted with recent admission for ecoli 
bacteremia, likely biliary source given cholangiocarcinoma and 
known mets, now s/p treatment with ertapenem ending on

ERCP during that admission showed tumor ingrowth 
within the duodenal stent.

Cannulation was not attempted during 
that admission.
In the ED, initial VS were 98.6 94 91/50 18 99% .

He was initially hypotensive on arrival, which resolved without 
any intervention to SBP 150.
Labs significant for WBC 9.6, H/H 11.5, 34.3, BMP WNL, ALT 77,
AST 142, alk phos 831, albumin 3.3, troponin .09.
Initial EKG reportedly without any concerning changes, however

EKG prior to transfer to the floor significant for t-wave 
inversions in V4-V6, new from prior.

Imaging significant for CT head showing left cerebellar infarct 
and right occipital that was not seen on CT of the head one 
month ago.

Neurology was consulted and recommended no 
intervention at this time.
Transfer VS were 96 141/73 17 100% RA

Upon arrival to the floor the patient states that he fell at 
home after he got up.

He states that he felt dizzy and nauseous 
and that he fell to the ground.

He loss consciousness and hits 
his head, but does not know how long he lost consciousness for.
He was found by ___, his ex-wife.

He denies chest pain or 
palpitations, loss of urinary or bowel incontinence.

He denies 
fevers or chills at home.
He does endorse significant depression and suicide ideation.

He 
states that he has a plan but refuses to share what his plan is.

He reports a prior suicide attempt of jumping out of a tree but 
does not elaborate further.

He denies any intentional ingestions 
or taking extra tylenol.
-- cholangiocarcinoma
-- s/p cholecystecomy in ___

-- s/p biliary stent in ___ for obstruction and pathology 
positive for recurrence
-- c/b gastric outlet obstruction s/p stenting

-- patient deferred anti-neoplastic therapy and XRT in the past, 
but recently was treated with stereotactic body radiotherapy,
2400 in three fractions, completed on ___.
-- Hypertension
-- diabetes
No history of cancer or strokes

Mr. ___ is a ___ with a PMHx of cholangiocarcinoma s/p 
resection ___ c/b cholangitis in ___ s/p biliary stent 
placement, local mets to duodenum s/p duodenal stent placement, 
completed Cyberknife treatment in ___, with recent admission 
for E.coli bacteremia, presented with syncopal episode vs 
mechanical fall, found down, found to have troponinemia and 
subacute cerebellar infarct.

EKG showed new lateral t-wave 
inversions, with troponin T peaking at 0.10.

CT scan showed 
subacute infarctions in the right occiptal lobe and left 
cerebellar hemisphere.

MRI/MRA confirmed numerous small 
scattered acute to subacute infarcts suggestive of embolic 
etiology.

Given his desires to maintain his quality of life, he 
was initiated on Lovenox for further stroke prevention.

However, 
as further discussions with the patient continued, he voiced his 
desires to be comfort measures only, so Lovenox was 
discontinued.
# Comfort Measures Only: In discussion with the patient on
___, he has decided to be comfort measures only.

The 
primary team mentioned that with blood draws, IV fluids, blood 
transfusions, possibly antibiotics and endoscopy there is a 
chance we could return his health to the state it was in before 
he came to the hospital, and that if we did nothing he may die 
in days to weeks.

He said that he would prefer to be 
comfortable and not have further labs and treatments intended to 
prolong life.

The above was later discussed with his ex-wife and 
son who felt that this was consistent with his wishes.

He was 
subsequently kept comfortable, with Tylenol, tramadol, and 
morphine PRN.

He was initiated on mirtazapine 7.5 mg qhs, to 
aide with sleep, which was subsequently discontinued due to 
daytime sleepiness.

He was continued on a bowel regimen to 
assist with abdominal pain.

# Subacute cerebellar infarct: CT scan significant for interval 
subacute infarctions in the right occipital lobe and left 
cerebellar hemisphere as well as a chronic-appearing infarction 
in the left cerebellar hemisphere.

Given discussion of patient's 
goals of care, who verbalizes that he would want any treatment 
that would maintain his quality of life without significant 
risk, the decision was made to initiate anticoagulation for 
stroke prevention, and the patient was started on Lovenox 
injections.

TTE without evidence of thrombus, although poor 
image.

After further discussions clarifying the patient's goal 
of care, he decided to be comfort measures only so Lovenox was 
discontinued.

# RUQ pain with transaminitis: ALT unchanged from prior, AST 142 
on admission, up from baseline ___, alkaline phosphatase 
elevated to 831, t. bili WNL, lipase WNL.

Recent ERCP showed 
tumor ingrowth of stent.

Gallbladder ultrasound upon admission 
significant for hepatitic metastases, without identification of 
the stent.
KUB showed presence of stents.

LFTS relatively stable 
during this hospitalization.
His abdominal pain was treated with
Tylenol, Zofran, and oxycodone.

He did not exhibit evidence of 
cholangitis and did not receive antibiotics this 
hospitalization.

Following goals of care discussion, management 
shifted to comfort focus and he recevied tramadol as needed for 
pain.

# Syncope: Patient presenting after being found down, without 
clear history, however, does give report of mechanical fall with 
precedent lightheadedness.

He was not altered at time of 
admission, however, multiple etiologies could explain either his 
fall or earlier confusion if present.

Given multiple lab 
abnormalities, likely toxic metabolic.

Urine/serum toxicology 
negative.

CT showing subacute cerebellar infarct, so balance or 
coordination issues could have contributed to mechanical fall.

He appeared dehydrated upon admission, with positive 
orthostatics, which improved with IV fluid.

# Troponinemia: Initial troponin of 0.09, EKG with new t-wave 
inversions in lateral precordial leads.
Repeat troponin of 0.08.

Could represent demand ischemia in the setting of medical 
illness, possible hypotension, or subacute stroke.

No known 
cardiac history.

# Oral candiasis: Patient was continued on nystatin QID for 
comfort.
